prompt:
Use case: photorealistic-natural. Create ONE highly refined NORMAL RECTILINEAR architectural interior photo in landscape3:2, output2048x1360 or largest available. Input1: current apartment360 panorama is GEOMETRY/ADJACENCY evidence ONLY, NOT output projection. Keep the existing floor plan, original doors/windows and all previously approved functional layouts. DO NOT output360/equirectangular/fisheye, a collage, curved walls, a board of samples, an exterior or a close-up that loses the room. Correct straight verticals and a real28-32mm architectural lens, plausible small-apartment proportions. Every visible edge, reveal, textile seam and fixture must look built, not generic CGI: fine open wood grain at realistic scale, tiny eased edge, satin non-plastic metal, actual separate fabric weave, coherent tiled joints, properly supported shelves, meaningful surface contact shadows. Natural soft NEUTRAL daylight plus just a few local warm task pools; readable white balance, no overall yellow/orange haze, HDR halos or artificial blur. No people, text, visible brand logos, watermarks or cloned botanical art everywhere. This is an original home design informed by published general design principles, not a reproduction of a designer's named project. THE USER EXPLICITLY WANTS INTENTIONAL OBJECT PLACEMENT AND SMALL LIVED-IN DECORATIONS: do not make an empty showroom. Group useful small personal items around actual daily activities, harmonize material/colour/height and leave working surfaces free. Don't randomly scatter repetitive props.
STYLE: deep walnut and muted smoked oak, warm-gray white plaster, olive linen and small burnt-sienna accent, paper/opal light, dark bronze, balanced clean daylight
LEARNED DESIGN PRIORITIES: Refine into a convincing Japanese mid-century home, not identical generic beige furniture. Walnut joinery with thin profiles and slim exposed timber rails, small recessed pulls, tactile wool rug with a subdued olive/rust geometric border rather than giant circles, simple hand-made ceramic, soft paper/opal lamps, low storage and generous empty working surfaces. Rectilinear aligned cabinet faces, thoughtful end grain and thin back panels, realistic small reveals. No RGB, no fake rice-paper entire walls or decorative beams.
EXACT LAYOUT: Original1.80m bed and entrance dressing zone, only original end exterior window, left side wall solid, wardrobes stay at entry, no added television, no fireplace, no bed facing invented window.
VISIBLE IMPROVEMENTS: Use an upholstered or timber-backed headboard with one readable material junction, small thin bedside ledge each side, individual downward reading light and discrete switch/charging, real duvet and linen seams, full-height closed wardrobe reveals and a reachable laundry pullout, mirror on actual solid panel, no bulky bench blocking foot route.
LIVED-IN STYLING: LIVED-IN STYLING: on one bedside ledge a small grouped tray holding reading book, tiny ceramic cup/water glass and charging phone placed neatly; another bedside gets only individual reading lamp and one small photo frame. Soft casually folded throw and two coordinated plain/stripe pillows, not a mountain of cushions. Wardrobe/dressing nook has contained jewelry/key dish, one small mirror and a linen laundry basket tucked at cabinet end, no random sculptures, perfume wall, plants around bed or clinical hotel staging.
CAMERA: Eye1.30m normal rectilinear28-32mm photo from original bedroom entry towards bed showing one part of dressing cabinetry and original window, natural proportions.
